cues.text: Start with Architecture: one unit is 30 centimetres. Use a half-unit grid for the partitions.
Draw the slab, forty-two by eighteen metres: 140 by 60 units.
Build one six metre square frame. Four corner columns come first, using Cuboid and axis helpers.
Nice. Add the beams at the column tops. Twelve units overall gives a height of 3.6 metres.
Window-select the frame and Make Object. Then Edit Prototype to define its array handle.
Place the hotspot above the second grid diagonal, on an axis helper. Choose Multiply Volumetric.
Attach every beam and column. Pick Reference at the far corner of the first six metre bay.
Good. Select the instance and drag its hotspot to the opposite corner of the slab.
Twenty-one structural modules: seven across and three deep, all driven by one instance hotspot.
For the core stairs, set flight height to six units and the step count to twelve.
Draw a rectangular contour C and Make Object, so the same outline can define both flights.
Add helpers for the contour copy and the landing. Copy the contour six units across and up.
Nice. Draw walking path P in the lower outline. Set C, then P, to create twelve risers.
Use the landing helpers at six units: half the 3.6 metre storey height.
Reverse the walking path in the upper contour, then set C and P for the return flight.
Hide Objects in the selection filters while drafting the core, to keep the floor grid accessible.
Select both flights and the landing. Move Copy places the second evacuation stair in the east bay.
Set partition thickness to half a unit: fifteen centimetres. The offset is a quarter unit.
Draw the two lift cases on the left of the central lift hall.
Move Copy repeats the partition assembly on the right: four lift cases around one shared hall.
Good. Parallel partitions separate the stair enclosures from their outer side halls.
Enclose the stair bays at north and south. The middle hall remains open at both ends.
To the west, divide the service bay into women's and men's toilets, accessed from the side hall.
To the east, put storage and copying north of the kitchen, then a meeting room in the end bay.
Cut the lift openings on the wall faces. Axis helpers carry their 2.1 metre heads.
Give each toilet its own door from the west side hall.
Good. Add doors between the side halls and the two protected staircase enclosures.
Storage and kitchen open from the east hall; the copier room connects through storage.
Door fits the first lift opening: ninety centimetres wide and 2.1 metres high.
Move Copy repeats that door. Use matching floor-grid references in the clear open space.
The meeting room gets a wider entrance from the north open space.
The east and west sides are plain walls, one unit thick: thirty centimetres, with no windows.
Label axes A to H and rows one to four. Each bay is six metres square.
Mark the lift and stair enclosures FR90, and the side halls FR30, following the plan.
Keep the north and south bands as open offices, connected around this central service core.
Show Objects and lock the labels. On a quarter-unit grid, build two mullions with no top rail.
Join their inner corners with a closed Polyline. The glazing fills the full height.
Make Object, and Edit Prototype. This panel is one and a half metres wide.
Add a Multiply Linear hotspot, attach the panel, and pick a reference one panel width back.
Nice. Drag the instance handle across the frontage: twenty-eight glazed panels.
Move the assembled curtain wall onto the south edge, using its corner and a helper.
Copy the wall to the north edge. Both facades share one definition. Then unlock the labels.
For the ceiling, make one reusable sixty centimetre square panel in the open office zone.
Edit Prototype. A volumetric array hotspot repeats the panel in both plan directions.
Drag the instance handle to form two rows of twenty panels, then lift the assembly on a helper.
Good. Seven by three structural bays, four lifts, two staircases and open offices around one central core.
The partial ceiling leaves the layout visible. The structural and facade grids remain hotspot-driven.
